sections.h2: Who handles your Union County tax bill
sections.html:
Union County Tax Administration runs property tax, and its Revenue Division collects the bills. The Revenue Division sits at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 119, Monroe. Mail goes to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111-0038, and the phone is 704-283-3848.

Valuation questions and appeals go to the Tax Administrator's Office at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 236, or 704-283-3746. To pay in person, use the collector's counter in the Government Center, open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning to 5:00 in the evening.

The county also collects for ten municipalities: Fairview, Hemby Bridge, Lake Park, Marshville, Marvin, Mineral Springs, Stallings, Waxhaw, Wesley Chapel and Wingate. A house in one of those towns gets a single combined bill through the county. If your parcel sits in a town that is not on that list, ask the county which office bills it.

Growth here is quick. The estimate is 267,674 residents in July 2025, up 12.4% from the April 2020 base, across 632.74 square miles of land, or 376.6 residents per square mile.

The median owned home is valued at $417,300 and 81.6% of homes are owner-occupied. The county counts 95,683 housing units as of July 2025, with 2,707 permits issued for 2025. Median rent is $1,496 and median household income is $102,900. Steady building and rising values mean your assessed value may have shifted a lot since you bought.

The most recent general reappraisal raised total taxable valuation from $32.38 billion in 2021 to $60.05 billion as of January 1, 2025, an increase of 60.05%. Residential value rose 63.45% and commercial and industrial value rose 45.59%.

Parcel counts grew from 104,057 in 2021 to 114,182 in 2025. The county's median home value went from $293,377 to $403,000.

Between reappraisals the county only sends a new notice when something changes on a property, such as new construction, an addition, demolition, a renovation, rezoning or an acreage change. North Carolina requires counties to reappraise every eighth year, so call the office to learn the next scheduled year.

Land and personal property bills come due September 1. Interest does not start until after January 5, and a mailed check is safe if its postmark is that day or earlier. When January 5 lands on a weekend, the cutoff moves to Monday.

On January 6 a 2% charge begins and runs to month end. After that, three-fourths of 1% is added every month. Vehicle tax is handled at plate registration or renewal, so you will not see it on this bill.

Call the office for this year's rate and ask whether a prepayment discount applies.

sections.h2: Other charges the Revenue Division collects
sections.html:
Property tax is only part of the division's workload. A closing agent may ask about any of these for the property you are selling.

  • Tax bills for land, buildings and business or personal property.
  • Delinquent motor vehicle tax bills.
  • Gross receipts taxes.
  • Current and delinquent water and sewer bills.
  • Landfill fees and other utility payments.

The division also values every registered motor vehicle owned by a county resident. For a house sale, call 704-283-3848 and ask whether any water, sewer or landfill balance sits on the account you are selling.

Union County accepts payment five ways.

  • Mail: use the return envelope or write to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111.
  • Drop box: on Stewart St. Extension, behind the Historic Post Office.
  • Phone: 1-855-497-0718.
  • Web: the county's pay online link.
  • Counter: the Government Center.

At a sale, your closing agent can settle the current bill so the property passes to the buyer free of tax debt. Have the closer ask the Revenue Division for a payoff number.

Begin with an informal review through Tax Administration. Still unhappy? Ask for a formal hearing in front of the county's equalization board. A staff appraiser reviews what you submit and mails a written decision. Return the form printed at the foot of that letter and the case moves up to the board.

Five local citizens sit on the board, listen to you and to the staff, and rule within 30 days. Still disagree? The board's letter lays out the next step, the statewide Property Tax Commission, and G.S. 105-290 allows 30 days from the mailing date of that notice.

Evidence that helps: appraisals as of the revaluation date, sales of similar properties, photos of unusual damage, and letters about septic limits from Environmental Health or a soil scientist. The percentage of change since a prior assessment cannot be considered. Neither stage costs a fee, and hiring a lawyer is optional. Windows to file follow the mailing of notices, so call Tax Administration to learn the dates that apply now.

sections.h2: Relief programs that can lower a bill
sections.html:
North Carolina gives three ways to cut a bill, and you can use just one of them. Ask for any of them from the county assessor on Form AV-9. The form for 2026 prints the income limit at $38,800 and the upper circuit breaker band at $58,200.

  • An elderly or disabled exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1C, which NCDOR says has no age or income cap.
  • The circuit breaker under G.S. 105-277.1B, which limits tax to a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

Ask Tax Administration which one fits and when to file. A sale ends eligibility for the circuit breaker, so deferred taxes become payable at closing.

Unpaid tax follows the land, not the owner. Under G.S. 105-355 the lien attaches as of the listing date and carries penalties, interest and costs, which is why buyers and their lenders want it paid off at closing.

If the bill stays unpaid, the county can file a foreclosure suit under G.S. 105-374 that ends with a public auction at the courthouse door. Redeeming before the sale is confirmed means paying the taxes along with penalties, interest and costs.

Order a payoff from the Revenue Division, have the closer send it from your sale proceeds, and hold on to the receipt. Deed stamp tax is its own charge against the seller, taken by the register of deeds when the deed is filed.

A cash sale skips the buyer's lender underwriting and appraisal. The tax payoff still comes out of your proceeds at closing, so ask the Revenue Division for the figure early and put it in writing with your closer. Also ask about water, sewer and landfill balances at the same time, since the division bills those too, and a surprise balance can delay a closing.

faqs.q: When does Union County need my tax payment?
faqs.a: Due September 1. Interest stays off until January 6, when 2% applies for the month, and three-fourths of 1% is added monthly after that.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Union County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Use the collector's counter at the Government Center, open weekdays 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Mailed payments go to the Monroe post office box.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Union County value?
faqs.a: Yes. An informal review with Tax Administration comes first, and an equalization board hearing is next if needed. Call 704-283-3746 for dates.

faqs.q: Does Union County have a veteran property tax exclusion?
faqs.a: Yes, for a qualifying disabled veteran: the first $45,000 of value is excluded. Apply through the county assessor.

faqs.q: Who owes deed stamp tax on a Union County sale?
faqs.a: Seller pays it, at the register's office before the deed is recorded. Check the settlement statement for the amount.
